clue.text: In skipping tutorial, boy gets round girl

indicators.note: the boy's name wraps itself around the trimmed tutorial word

parts.note: Roy is a boy's name

indicators.note: skipping means leaving out, so the word In is dropped from the tutorial

parts.note: a seminar is a tutorial-style class
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy dodging his class to spend time with a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skipping' suggests a rope game or skipping class, but here it means leaving out IN, which gives SEMAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Overthrow of monarch sure to have an adverse effect

indicators.note: an overthrow turns the monarch upside down, so in a down clue the letters are read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch
bound to happen means sure to happen

explanation.surface: Toppling a king is bound to backfire.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rebounds on you comes back to harm you, an idiom for backfiring.

clue.text: Way to address gentleman convict finally released from jail?

indicators.note: the last letter of convict is let out of the jail word

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word convict

explanation.surface: How to speak to a gentleman prisoner on his release.
explanation.walkthrough: STIR is British slang for prison; losing T, convict's last letter, leaves the title.
explanation.definitionFit: A knighted man or any gentleman is addressed with this courtesy title.

clue.text: Effeminate fellows accepting help, as it were

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the fellows hold the help

parts.note: fellows are men
aid is help
like is used informally as a filler meaning as it were

explanation.surface: Effeminate men being given assistance, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe manner suited to a young unmarried woman, so they are near synonyms.

clue.text: Falsify papers for firm

parts.note: to rig a result is to falsify it
ID, identity documents, are papers

explanation.surface: Forging documents on behalf of a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a noun (company) but is the adjective meaning stiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm in the sense of stiff and unbending is a synonym.

clue.text: Tyrant executes leading journalist coming from the East

indicators.note: in an across entry, coming from the east means read right to left

parts.note: to top someone is slang for killing them
an editor, ED, is the leading journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: A tyrant has a senior newspaperman put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executes' looks like 'carries out' but means TOPS, slang for kills; 'coming from the East' reverses TOPSED.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler who wields power cruelly is a synonym for tyrant.

clue.text: Genuine German dramatist, not British

indicators.note: not British means the abbreviation for British is removed

parts.note: Bertolt Brecht was a German playwright

explanation.surface: A true German playwright rather than a British one.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt is a German loanword in English meaning authentic or real.

clue.text: Like a fat cat or dog roaming Arctic?

parts.note: Pluto is Mickey Mouse's dog in the Disney cartoons

indicators.note: roaming means wandering about, so the letters of Arctic are moved around

explanation.surface: A cat or a dog wandering the frozen north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fat cat' sets up an animal scene, but means a rich person.
explanation.definitionFit: A fat cat is a wealthy, powerful person, and plutocratic describes rule or behaviour of the rich.

clue.text: Archer is about right, training climbers on it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so Archer and is go around the letter for right

parts.note: William Tell, the legendary Swiss archer

explanation.surface: An archer is training plants up a support, apparently right about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archer' looks like the radio soap family but is William Tell.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice frame on which climbing plants are trained and supported.

clue.text: Porter, possibly, outside a large house where nuts may be stored

indicators.note: outside means wrapping around the other pieces

parts.note: Cole Porter, the American songwriter; possibly marks the first name as one example

explanation.surface: A doorman stands outside a big house where nuts are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' suggests a squirrel's hoard, but these are coal nuts, small lumps of coal; 'Porter' suggests a doorman.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal cellar holds lumps of fuel, including the small pieces called nuts.

clue.text: Welsh actor eating fish and game in artists' place …

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the actor's name holds the fish

parts.note: Richard Burton was a Welsh actor
ling is a sea fish
house is another name for bingo

explanation.surface: A Welsh actor feasting on fish and playing a game where artists gather.
explanation.walkthrough: HOUSE is the game better known as bingo or housey-housey.
explanation.definitionFit: This Piccadilly mansion houses the Royal Academy of Arts, a home for artists.

clue.text: … will dine out in posh eatery at last, awkwardly

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the two letters around them

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of eatery
out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dining out in a smart restaurant, someone eats clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns WILL DINE into NWIELDIL, which goes 'in' between U and Y, the last letter of eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwieldily means in a cumbersome, hard-to-handle way, close in sense to awkwardly.

clue.text: Shrub wife planted on grassy area south of Bury?

indicators.note: planted on means set on top of what follows
south of means below in a down entry

parts.note: to inter is to bury
a green is a grassy area

explanation.surface: A wife puts a shrub on the village green in the town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the Lancashire town, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen plant from which oil is extracted; it is a low shrub.

clue.text: At school it may be called a cylindrical moulding

definitions.text: At school it may be called
definitions.meaning: the register of pupils is read out each morning
an architectural moulding shaped like a rounded rod

explanation.surface: At school it may be called a cylindrical moulding.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both the class register that is called and a rounded architectural moulding.

clue.text: Way to frame remark about airmen's proficiency in fencing?

indicators.note: to frame means to enclose, so the street letters go round the rest

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
a word is a remark
C, circa, means about
the RAF is the Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: A way to set a comment about airmen who are good with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill with a sword is skill in fencing.

clue.text: Occupied area of England once, and most of Wales, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means strangely arranged, so the letters are shuffled
most of drops the final letter of Wales

explanation.surface: A former territory in England, together with much of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' suggests alternate letters but is an anagram of AND + WALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of England under Danish law and control in Viking times.

clue.text: Moderate Tories protecting secure wildlife reserve

indicators.note: protecting means guarding by surrounding

parts.note: wets were moderate Conservatives opposed to Thatcher's policies
to land something is to secure it

explanation.surface: Moderate Conservatives safeguarding a nature reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics 'wets' were the moderate Conservatives in Thatcher's cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshes and fens are often protected habitats, serving as wildlife reserves.

clue.text: Forth — a river surrounded by rolling downs?

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the first pieces inside the shuffled hills
rolling means tumbling about, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The Forth, a river among rolling hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forth' looks like the Scottish river but means forward; DOWNS, the rolling chalk hills of southern England, rearrange around A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Forth means forwards, as in go forth.

clue.text: Sound made by simple feline, one living in burrow

indicators.note: sound made by tells us to say the words aloud

parts.note: mere means simple, plus cat for a feline

explanation.surface: A noise from a cat, an animal that lives underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A small African mongoose that lives in colonies in burrows.

clue.text: Hot stuff gathered for inspection, do we hear?

indicators.note: do we hear says the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: troops are mustered when assembled for inspection

explanation.surface: Is spicy food assembled to be checked?
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent condiment, so a hot substance.

clue.text: Capricious European kings, Greek by the sound of it

parts.note: R, rex, for king, doubled for kings

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: Attic means of Athens, hence Greek

explanation.surface: Fickle European monarchs who sound Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpredictable and changeable behaviour is erratic.

clue.text: Male Anglicans on time to welcome Liberal pope

indicators.note: to welcome means to take in, so the men of the church hold the Liberal

parts.note: CE, the Church of England, plus men

explanation.surface: Anglican men welcoming a liberal pontiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Several popes took the name Clement, so it is one example.

clue.text: Cereal having a certain appeal before work

indicators.note: before puts the appeal letters ahead of the work

parts.note: SA is sex appeal
go means work, as in function

explanation.surface: A breakfast food with an appeal before work.
explanation.definitionFit: A starch from palm pith, used in puddings and counted as a cereal food.

clue.text: Adequate set of songs about youngster's first transport

indicators.note: about means around, so these pieces surround the youngster's opening letter

parts.note: fair means adequate
a song cycle is a set of songs

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of youngster

explanation.surface: Decent songs about a child's first vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's small bicycle of the old days is a form of transport.

clue.text: Arrive at range

definitions.meaning: extent or scope, as in out of range

explanation.definitionFit: Getting to a place, and the distance one can extend, share one word.

clue.text: Some cherish a longing for a saint's aura

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some long for the glow of sainthood.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'for', but 'for' is the link word joining wordplay to definition; 'a saint's aura' alone substitutes for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle of light round a saint's head in paintings is that aura.

clue.text: Chap with friend, one touring 10, a broadcasting centre once

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the pieces go around what 10 stands for

parts.note: Alex is a man's name
and means with
a pal is a friend
an ace is a one in cards
Burlington House is home to the Royal Academy, RA

explanation.surface: A man and his friend, one of them visiting the gallery, at the old broadcast site.
explanation.walkthrough: The RA is the Royal Academy, housed at 10's Burlington House.
explanation.definitionFit: This north London building was the BBC's early television transmitting site.

clue.text: Remains found in wood

explanation.definitionFit: Both the residue of a fire and a tree's timber share one word.

clue.text: New judge attends function taking place in tower

indicators.note: attends means is present at, so the pieces sit inside the occasion

parts.note: a do is a party or function
on means happening

explanation.surface: A newly appointed judge goes to a function in a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The keep of a castle, its central fortified tower.

clue.text: Husband long constrained by spiteful woman's gossip

indicators.note: constrained by means held within

parts.note: a cat is a spiteful woman; the 's stands for is
to itch is to long for

explanation.surface: A spiteful woman's gossip about a husband's longing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle talk or light conversation is a form of gossip.
